rationale: Abstract 134 discusses clinical drooling in a Parkinson cohort and abstract 148 uses saliva as a biomarker specimen. The numbered presentations provide no raw-fig exposure and graded Parkinson drooling comparison.
The Control ID anchored blocks include isolated saliva, dry mouth and acute drooling findings in other clinical settings. No member supplies a raw-fig Parkinson symptom comparison.

The 964-page original has adjacent esophageal clearance and foreign-body cases. The fig token matches numbered figures or part of an author contact string, while the outcomes concern other exposures and populations.

The 180 numbered meeting parts include saliva and drooling in distinct clinical populations, including ALS or mucopolysaccharidosis cases. No culinary fig exposure or Parkinson drooling measure was assigned.
Retrieved the complete 42-page PDF. Nascimento's S69 review compares the properties of drooling scales and has a matching journal article. The proceedings provide no tested raw-fig intervention.

Retrieved the complete 60-page PDF and examined image-only S22. The Battel poster studies saliva residue and the journal companion tabulates a separate self-rated drooling outcome. Labeit studies swallowing initiation. Neither assigns raw fig.
This article reviews growth-hormone secretagogues in ALS. Sialorrhea appears in clinical management background for a different disease.

The preliminary Padua proceedings include saliva as a biomarker specimen. Titles and source context distinguish the pre-meeting edition and the later expanded collection. There is no raw fig and measured Parkinson drooling comparison.

Table 1 gives an item-level drooling group comparison, and both original supplemental PDFs were verified. The study concerns functional connectivity in Parkinson disease and controls, without a food intervention.
The review evaluates clinical toxicity and reported adverse events for cannabidiol. It supplies no raw-fig exposure comparison or graded Parkinson drooling outcome.
The original familial Lewy body case series records drooling in two people with a severe neurological syndrome. It provides clinical observations and no defined food exposure or drooling comparison.
The paper studies health-service use and costs in progressive supranuclear palsy. Sialorrhea appears as a possible symptom in a different population.

The Spanish scale validation reports Spearman r=0.50 between its gastrointestinal domain and the separate MDS-UPDRS saliva and drooling item. The erratum changes a discussion sentence. Both sources supply instrument context and no dietary comparison.
The niacin narrative concerns several neurological conditions and includes sialorrhea in other clinical context. It does not report a raw-fig comparison.
The expanded Padua proceedings include shifted or repeated abstract numbering and salivary exercise biomarker findings. The studies do not measure Parkinson drooling after eating raw fig.
The scoping review describes drooling among reported symptoms or medication outcomes for ADCY5-related movement disorder. The population and exposures differ from the claim.

The Parkinson model study uses a plant-derived preparation and a drug combination distinct from culinary fig. Its introduction names sialorrhea; the model results do not evaluate a raw-fig change in clinical drooling.
The review concerns sensory neuropathy in ALS and names sialorrhea in background. There is no raw-fig exposure and Parkinson drooling outcome comparison.
The original case describes sialorrhea and dysphagia with oral squamous-cell carcinoma. It supplies clinical diagnostic context and no Parkinson or raw-fig comparison.
The advanced dementia report lists drooling among medication adverse events in observational treatment series. The report does not evaluate raw fig or a Parkinson-specific drooling outcome.

The prospective iRBD study reports more drooling at follow-up in the mixed neurodegeneration group. Both original text and workbook were verified. The follow-up item has four and nine nonblank entries and no analyzed fig exposure.
The original JATS proceedings separate the drooling lecture from other numbered reports. Its discussion distinguishes saliva production and clearance without testing a raw-fig exposure.
